cluster.confirmScaleZero: Scale "{{name}}" to 0 replicas? This will stop the deployment.

events.truncated: Showing only the 200 most recent events matching the filter

cluster.namespaceAgeHint: Sorted newest to oldest: the ones created by the cluster deployment are all born at the same time.
cluster.confirmRollback: Roll "{{name}}" back to the previous revision?
cluster.confirmDelete: You are about to DELETE "{{name}}". This cannot be undone. Type the exact name to confirm:
cluster.confirmDrain: You are about to DRAIN node "{{name}}": it will be marked unschedulable and all its pods evicted (except DaemonSets). Type the exact name to confirm:
cluster.drainResult: Drain requested: {{evicted}} pods evicted, {{skipped}} skipped (DaemonSet/static), {{failed}} failed.

resources.unavailable: This resource type is not available in the cluster
resources.unavailableHint: Almost always the technical ServiceAccount's ClusterRole lacks the permission: re-apply deploy/rbac/serviceaccount.yaml in the cluster. Other resources are not affected.
resources.secretsHint: Only type and keys are listed. Values are visible only to a cluster administrator when opening the YAML, and that is audited.

helm.catalogHint: Charts from the configured repositories. Installing runs a server dry-run before applying.
helm.reposHint: Chart repositories (HTTP with index.yaml, or OCI). Platform-wide: the same catalog serves every cluster.
helm.confirmDeleteRepo: Remove repository "{{name}}" from the catalog? Installed releases are not affected.
helm.noRepos: No chart repositories yet. An administrator can add them under Administration → Helm repositories.
helm.confirmUninstall: You are about to UNINSTALL release "{{name}}" and all its resources. Type the exact name to confirm:
helm.dryRunOk: The cluster accepts {{chart}} {{version}}. Manifests that would be applied:
helm.noReleases: No Helm releases in the selected namespaces.

gitops.title: GitOps
gitops.hint: Manifests from a git repository applied to the cluster periodically or on webhook (server-side apply). With "prune", what disappears from the repo is deleted from the cluster; without it, it is not.
gitops.tokenHint: For private repos over HTTPS, a personal access token with read permission; stored encrypted.
gitops.lastApplied: Objects applied in the last sync
gitops.confirmDelete: Remove source "{{name}}"? Resources already applied in the cluster are kept.
gitops.webhookHint: To sync on push, configure this webhook in the git provider: in GitLab set the token as “Secret token”; in GitHub/Gitea/Bitbucket as “Secret” (HMAC body signature). It never goes in the URL. The token is shown only now: save it.
gitops.webhookTokenHidden: The token was shown only when the source was created.
gitops.empty: No GitOps sources in this cluster.
gitops.sshHint: URL like git@github.com:org/repo.git or ssh://… The key is stored encrypted. known_hosts is required: paste the output of "ssh-keyscan <host>" so the git server is verified (without it, anyone on the network could serve manifests to the cluster).
gitops.kustomize: Build with Kustomize (kustomization.yaml in the path)
gitops.pruneHint: Prune: applied objects carry the bayplan.io/gitops-source label and, after each successful sync, those carrying it that are no longer in the repo are deleted from the cluster.

fleet.title: Needs attention
fleet.subtitle: Issues across all the clusters you have access to
fleet.allGood: No cluster has issues right now
fleet.disconnectedWarning_one: {{count}} cluster is not responding ({{clusters}}): there is no way to know whether it has issues.
fleet.disconnectedWarning_other: {{count}} clusters are not responding ({{clusters}}): there is no way to know whether they have issues.

overview.title: Overview
overview.error: The cluster overview could not be loaded
overview.oldestNodeHint: Age of the oldest node, the closest thing to the cluster's age that the API exposes
overview.capacityHint: Sum of requests, not actual usage

clusterAdmin.title: Managed clusters
clusterAdmin.saTokenHint: Generated with: kubectl create token <sa> -n kube-system --duration=87600h, after applying deploy/rbac/serviceaccount.yaml.
clusterAdmin.error: The cluster could not be added
clusterAdmin.confirmDeleteBody: You are about to delete "{{name}}". Its per-cluster role assignments and SSO group mappings will also be removed. If this is a mistake, you will have to onboard the cluster again and grant those permissions again. Type the exact name to confirm.
clusterAdmin.empty: No clusters have been configured yet.
clusterAdmin.connectionHint: Leave as is to keep the connection untouched. If you fill in a credential it is validated against the cluster and replaces the current one, keeping granted permissions.
clusterAdmin.kubeconfigHint: Paste the full kubeconfig (kubectl config view --raw --flatten). Only embedded data works: an exec plugin (aws, gcloud, az) cannot run on the server.
clusterAdmin.insecureHint: Lab use only: without a CA any intermediary can impersonate the cluster.
clusterAdmin.agentHint: Recommended. The server does not need to reach the API server: an agent deployed in the cluster opens an outbound connection (WebSocket) and the server operates through it. Works for clusters behind NAT, on another network or with a private endpoint; no CA or token to paste, and the agent keeps its RBAC and its version up to date by itself.
clusterAdmin.agentHint2: On creation you get a kubectl apply command that installs the agent with all its RBAC. Requires the public URL set in Settings.
clusterAdmin.agentInsecure: The agent will not verify the server's TLS certificate
clusterAdmin.agentNeverSeen: Agent not connected yet: apply the manifest
clusterAdmin.onboardingHint: Run this with a cluster-admin kubeconfig. It installs the namespace, ServiceAccount, RBAC, the agent credential and its Deployment. As soon as the agent connects, the cluster turns "Connected".
clusterAdmin.onboardingExpires: The manifest URL expires at {{when}}. Afterwards regenerate it with the "Manifest" button (the agent credential does not change).
clusterAdmin.dockerHint: Docker or Podman host (standalone or Swarm). The agent runs as a container on the host with the socket mounted and exposes it to the server through the tunnel: containers, images, volumes and networks, with logs and terminal.
clusterAdmin.dockerHint2: On creation you get a docker run command to execute on the host. Requires the public URL set in Settings.
clusterAdmin.onboardingDockerHint: Run this on the Docker/Podman host (with access to the socket). The agent key is inside the command: treat it as a secret. As soon as the agent connects, the environment turns "Connected".
clusterAdmin.cloudHint: The server describes the cluster in the provider (endpoint and CA) and authenticates with short-lived tokens from the credential. It must reach the API server endpoint; for private clusters use the agent.
clusterAdmin.cloudNoCredentials: No cloud credentials. Create one in
clusterAdmin.cloudNoneFound: The credential cannot see any cluster.
clusterAdmin.cloudRbac: RBAC to apply on the cluster
clusterAdmin.cloudOnboardingHint: The cluster is connected with the credential identity, but that identity has no Kubernetes permissions until you apply this RBAC (unless it already is cluster-admin, like the creator of an EKS cluster). Until then reads return 403.
clusterAdmin.cloudStepAws: Map the IAM principal {{identity}} to the group {{group}} with an access entry (or in the aws-auth ConfigMap):
clusterAdmin.cloudStepAzure: The YAML grants permissions to the service principal by its object id ({{identity}}). If the cluster uses Azure RBAC for Kubernetes, it also needs the "Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Reader" role or higher.
clusterAdmin.cloudStepGcp: The YAML grants permissions to the service account {{identity}}. The SA also needs container.clusters.get in IAM to reach the API server.
clusterAdmin.cloudStepApply: Apply the RBAC with a cluster-admin kubeconfig: kubectl apply -f bayplan-rbac.yaml
clusterAdmin.rbacScopedHint: Only what the panel reads plus three write roles. The agent keeps its own RBAC up to date; direct clusters need it re-applied when the panel is updated.
clusterAdmin.rbacClusterAdminHint: The agent and panel admins get cluster-admin. Editors and read-only stay scoped. Nothing ever needs re-applying.

userAdmin.title: Users and roles
userAdmin.error: The role could not be granted
userAdmin.createError: The user could not be created
userAdmin.confirmDelete: Delete user "{{username}}"? Their permissions and sessions will also be removed. This cannot be undone.
userAdmin.actionError: The action on the user could not be completed

access.title: Effective permissions
access.hint: What this user can actually do on each cluster, combining their global role with per-cluster assignments (the highest privilege wins).

from.both: Global and cluster (both must be revoked)

roleHint.admin: everything, including delete, drain and terminal
roleHint.editor: deploy, scale, restart and apply YAML

groupMappings.title: SSO group mappings
groupMappings.subtitle: Translates membership in an identity provider (OIDC) group into an application role. It is the only source of permissions for SSO sign-in.
groupMappings.noMappingsWarning: SSO is configured but there are no mappings: every SSO sign-in of a user without a manual role assignment will fail with "no_role_mapped", even if the identity provider accepts their credentials.
groupMappings.adGroupIdHint: The group's identifier exactly as the identity provider sends it in the groups claim. In Entra ID it is the group's Object ID, unless your tenant emits a different identifier (for example the sAMAccountName of a synced group).
groupMappings.confirmDelete: Delete the mapping of group {{group}} with role "{{role}}"? Users who depend only on it will lose access at their next sign-in.
groupMappings.createError: The mapping could not be created
groupMappings.deleteError: The mapping could not be deleted

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Instance configuration. Applied live, no restart needed.

server.title: Server
server.hint: How this instance is reached from outside.
server.publicURLHint: Used to build the SSO redirect URI and absolute links. It must be the URL users open the application with, including the TLS proxy.
server.agentImageHint: Empty = the image of the same version as this server ({{version}}): {{image}}. Agents upgrade themselves to the version the server publishes (same repository, different tag). Change it only if you publish the image in your own registry.
server.agentCACertHint: PEM of the CA that signs the public URL's certificate when it is not a public CA (an ingress with a corporate CA, cert-manager's self-signed issuer). Agents trust it on top of the system CAs and keep verifying the server.
server.agentCACertBuiltin: This server already knows the CA of its certificate (its own self-signed HTTPS or the chart's cert-manager CA) and puts it in every agent manifest. Fill this in only if the public URL goes through another certificate.

oidc.title: Single sign-on (OIDC)
oidc.hint: Any OpenID Connect provider: Entra ID, Keycloak, Okta, Google… Roles are granted per group under “SSO groups”.
oidc.groupsClaimHint: Leave empty if the provider does not emit groups: then only users with a manually assigned role can sign in.
oidc.graphFallback: Resolve groups through Microsoft Graph when the token lacks them
oidc.graphFallbackHint: Entra ID only. Needed above ~200 groups (distributed claim). Requires the GroupMember.Read.All permission.
oidc.redirectURIHint: Register it verbatim in the identity provider. The /api prefix is part of the real path.

smtp.title: Outgoing mail (SMTP)
smtp.hint: Mail server for email notification channels. Port 465 = implicit TLS; 587 with STARTTLS.
smtp.insecure: Do not verify the mail server certificate (lab only)

costs.title: Costs
costs.hint: Unit prices to estimate cost per namespace (Costs tab of each cluster). One rate for the whole instance; 0 = not configured.

ai.title: AI (Explain)
ai.hint: LLM provider behind the "Explain" button: one per instance, paid with your organization's key. Calls are made by the server, never by the browser.
ai.modelHint: As your account or server names it.
ai.baseURLHint: Empty = api.openai.com/v1. For a self-hosted model, its OpenAI-compatible URL (e.g. http://ollama:11434/v1): then nothing leaves your network.
ai.apiKeySet: A key is stored; leave empty to keep it.
ai.minRoleHint: It sends cluster data to the provider and spends money: editor by default.
ai.dailyLimitHint: Counted before calling the provider; if the counter cannot be read, the call is refused.
ai.privacy: What is sent: the object's YAML without env values, Secret data or managedFields, its recent events and the last log lines of the container in trouble, with secret-looking values scrubbed. Never the panel's own namespace. Every call is audited.
ai.testFailed: The test could not be run

agents.title: Agents
agents.hint: Image the cluster agents run and the CA they trust to reach this server.

audit.title: Audit
audit.subtitle: Who did what, when and with what result. Includes denied attempts and changes made directly through SQL.

profile.title: Profile
profile.saveError: Your profile details could not be saved
profile.ssoManaged: Your name and email are managed by the identity provider and refreshed on every sign-in.
profile.preferencesHint: They are stored in your account, so they follow you to any browser.

yaml.title: YAML
yaml.editing: Editing — changes are validated by the cluster before applying
yaml.dryRunOk: The cluster accepts the YAML. Applying it would:

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.description: The address you reached does not exist or the resource is no longer available.

cloud.title: Cloud credentials
cloud.description: AWS, Azure and Google Cloud credentials. The panel uses them to discover EKS/AKS/GKE clusters and connect with short-lived tokens issued by the provider: no CA or token to paste per cluster, and rotating the credential rotates all of its clusters.
cloud.regionsHint: EKS is regional: comma-separated regions to search for clusters.
cloud.inUse: It has clusters attached: delete them first.
cloud.rotateHint: If you change the secret it is validated with the provider and used on the next token refresh of its {{count}} clusters.

hint.aws: Access key of an IAM user or role with eks:ListClusters and eks:DescribeCluster. To operate, the principal needs an access entry on each cluster (shown when adding it).
hint.azure: Service principal (app registration) with the "Azure Kubernetes Service Cluster User" role on the subscription or the clusters. Requires clusters with Entra ID integration, or local accounts enabled.
hint.gcp: JSON key of a service account with the "Kubernetes Engine Cluster Viewer" role (container.clusters.get/list) on the project.

notify.title: Notifications
notify.description: Slack, Teams, webhook or email alerts for the problems the panel detects (CrashLoopBackOff, stalled rollouts, nodes down…) and for lost cluster connections. The same as "Needs attention", without having to look at it.

channelHint.slack: Slack Incoming Webhook (api.slack.com/apps → Incoming Webhooks). The URL is the secret: stored encrypted and never shown again.
channelHint.teams: Teams incoming webhook or Power Automate flow "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received". An Adaptive Card is sent.
channelHint.webhook: POST with a flat JSON (event, severity, cluster, kind, namespace, name, reason, detail, title, text, url, timestamp). Optionally an authentication header.
channelHint.email: Plain-text email to the recipients. Requires the SMTP server configured in Settings → Outgoing mail.

notify.error: The operation could not be completed
notify.noChannels: No channels. Add one to be able to create rules.
notify.confirmDeleteChannel: Delete channel "{{name}}"? It will be removed from the rules that use it.
notify.ruleHint: A rule picks which problems to notify and to which channels. The minimum duration avoids alerting on every normal rollout; the cooldown avoids repeating the same problem.
notify.insecure: Do not verify the webhook TLS certificate (lab only)

registries.title: Image registries
registries.description: Private registry credentials (Docker Hub, GHCR, Harbor, Quay, ACR…). They are platform-wide: from each cluster you bind them to the namespaces you need and the panel creates the dockerconfigjson Secret there. Rotating the credential updates every copy.
registries.clusterHint: Registries distributed to namespaces of this cluster as kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secrets. Re-synced every 15 minutes and when the credential is rotated.
registries.insecure: Do not verify the registry TLS certificate (lab only)
registries.nameHint: Lowercase, digits and hyphens. Names the Secret: bayplan-registry-<name>.
registries.addHint: The credential is checked against the registry before saving. For ECR use AWS as username and a token from `aws ecr get-login-password` (expires after 12 h).
registries.error: The operation could not be completed
registries.confirmDelete: Delete registry "{{name}}"? Its {{count}} Secrets will be removed from the clusters.
registries.deleted: Registry deleted. Secrets removed: {{removed}}; not removed: {{failed}}.
registries.rotateHint: Saving re-syncs the {{count}} bound namespaces with the new credential.
registries.noBindings: No registry bound to this cluster.
registries.noRegistries: No image registries configured. An administrator can add them in
registries.attachDefaultSA: Add to imagePullSecrets of the default ServiceAccount
registries.attachDefaultSAHint: Pods without serviceAccountName use it automatically. Otherwise pods must reference the Secret in imagePullSecrets.
registries.bindSyncFailed: Binding created, but the sync failed: {{error}}
registries.confirmUnbind: Remove "{{name}}" from namespace {{namespace}}? The Secret will be deleted from the cluster.

quota.title: Namespace quota
quota.pageHint: Per-namespace caps (ResourceQuota) and per-container defaults (LimitRange). "Namespace quota" configures both at once, with a dry run first.
quota.hint: Creates or updates the ResourceQuota bayplan-quota and the LimitRange bayplan-limits of the namespace. Other quotas in the namespace are left alone. Kubernetes quantities: 2, 500m, 4Gi. Empty = no cap.
quota.createNamespace: Namespace "{{namespace}}" does not exist: create it
quota.limitsHint: Sum over all pods in the namespace. A pod exceeding them is not scheduled (the API server rejects it with the reason).
quota.defaultsHint: Applied to containers that declare no resources; without them, with an active CPU/memory quota those pods are rejected.
quota.partialDryRun: The namespace does not exist yet: the quota and LimitRange could not be dry-run on the server; they will be created along with it.

kubectl.title: kubectl shell
kubectl.hint: Real kubectl run on the server with your identity (cluster admin group). Every command is audited. No access to the server system: kubectl only.
kubectl.unavailable: The shell is not available: kubectl is not installed on the server or you lack permission.
kubectl.adminOnly: The kubectl shell requires the admin role on this cluster.
kubectl.help1: kubectl web shell. Only kubectl (alias: k) is accepted against this cluster, with your identity.
kubectl.help2: Local commands: help, clear, exit. History: ↑/↓. Ctrl+C aborts the running command.
kubectl.help3: Not available: proxy, port-forward, cp, edit, config; -f/--from-file only with "-" (stdin).
kubectl.help4: Examples: kubectl get pods -A · kubectl logs -f deploy/api · kubectl exec -it api-0 -- sh

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.hint: For scripts and CI: Authorization: Bearer bpl_…. A token acts with your permissions; a read-only one can only read. See the
tokens.error: The operation could not be completed
tokens.readOnlyHint: Recommended for automations that only query: no write route will work even if you are admin.
tokens.confirmRevoke: Revoke token "{{name}}"? Scripts using it will stop working.
tokens.createdHint: Copy it now: it will not be shown again. Treat it like a password.
tokens.mcpUsage: Connect an AI client (MCP), for example Claude Code:
tokens.mcpHint: Other clients (Codex, Cursor…): MCP server over HTTP at {{url}} with the same header. The AI acts with this token's permissions; a read-only token only gets the read tools.

apiDocs.title: API
apiDocs.authHint: Authenticate with a personal API token in the Authorization header (create it in your profile) or with the browser session cookie plus X-CSRF-Token on writes. Tokens in

backups.title: Backups
backups.hint: Backups of the cluster CONFIGURATION (deployments, services, configmaps, quotas, ingresses…) stripped of status, into an S3 bucket, with schedule and retention. They do not copy volumes: for PVC data use Velero or your storage snapshots.
backups.targetsHint: S3-compatible buckets (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph RGW…) where backups are stored. Adding one checks access and write; a missing bucket is created if allowed.
backups.adminOnly: Backups require the admin role on this cluster.
backups.insecure: Do not verify the endpoint TLS certificate (lab only)
backups.error: The operation could not be completed
backups.targetInUse: It has schedules: delete them first.
backups.confirmDeleteTarget: Delete target "{{name}}"? Uploaded backups stay in the bucket.
backups.noTargetsHint: No S3 targets configured. An administrator can add them in
backups.includeSecretsHint: Unchecked, Secrets keep their keys but not their values (not restorable). Checked, the bucket holds credentials: protect it accordingly.
backups.noSchedules: No schedules: no backups are taken.
backups.confirmDeleteSchedule: Delete schedule "{{name}}"? History is lost; bucket objects are kept.
backups.restoreHint: Pick the objects to apply to the cluster (server-side apply, with your identity). A dry run comes first; what you can restore is decided by the cluster RBAC.
backups.restoreNoSecrets: This backup was taken without Secret values: Secrets cannot be restored from it.

server.title: Backup of Bayplan itself
server.hint: A dump of Bayplan's own database (users, permissions, clusters, settings, audit log) to one of these targets on a schedule, or downloaded now. The encryption key is not inside: keep it apart, a restore needs both.
server.unavailable: pg_dump is not available on this server (the official image includes it).
server.restoreHint: Restoring is done from the command line into an empty database: see "Backing up Bayplan itself" in deploy/README.md.

images.title: Images
images.hint: Images in use in the cluster and their vulnerability scan (Trivy {{version}} on the server). A scan is shared by every cluster using the same image; scanned images are re-checked weekly because the CVE database changes.
images.unavailable: Trivy is not installed on the server: the image inventory is listed, but images cannot be scanned (TRIVY_PATH).
images.queued: Queued {{queued}} of {{requested}} images (those scanned less than an hour ago are skipped).
images.empty: No pods with images in this selection.

extensions.title: UI extensions
extensions.description: Links to external tools (Grafana, Kibana, Harbor…) shown in each cluster's menu, opened in a new tab or embedded in the panel. They are not plugins: the panel only builds the URL from the cluster context.
extensions.urlHint: Placeholders: {cluster} (name), {clusterId} and {namespace} (first namespace of the filter, empty if none).
extensions.embedHint: To be embedded, the tool must allow frames from the panel's domain (X-Frame-Options / CSP frame-ancestors). Otherwise the frame stays blank and only "open in new tab" works.
extensions.embedNote: Embedded external tool. If it stays blank, it does not allow frames: open it in a new tab.
extensions.notFound: Extension not found or not allowed to see it.

costs.title: Costs
costs.hint: Allocation estimate per namespace from the prices in Settings: reserved (requests) and, with metrics-server, used. It is not the provider's invoice.
costs.notConfigured: No prices configured: the table shows resources but no amounts. Set them in
costs.noMetrics: No real usage: {{reason}}. Only reserved resources are billed.
costs.prices: Prices: {{cpu}} {{currency}} per core·hour, {{mem}} {{currency}} per GiB·hour; {{hours}} h month.

metricsServer.title: Install metrics-server
metricsServer.hint: Applies the official kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server components.yaml (version pinned in the panel) with your identity, after a server dry-run. It provides real CPU and memory usage; without it only reserved resources are shown.
metricsServer.insecureHint: Needed on kubeadm, kind and most labs; without it metrics-server starts but collects nothing. Not needed on GKE/EKS/AKS.
metricsServer.installed: metrics-server {{version}} applied. Metrics will show up in a minute or two.
metricsServer.fallback: If it is a permissions error (scoped mode without re-applying RBAC), download the manifest and apply it with kubectl apply -f.
metricsServer.partialDryRun: Bindings to roles created in this same manifest cannot be dry-run on the server (the role does not exist yet in a dry-run); they will be created with the rest.

detail.notFound: This resource no longer exists in the cluster.
detail.notFoundHint: It may have been deleted or renamed. The list shows the current state.
detail.noEvents: No recent events for this resource.

topology.title: Topology
topology.hint: How the objects relate: Ingress → Service → workload → pods → volumes. Configured relations, not observed traffic.
topology.error: The topology could not be loaded
topology.tooLarge: {{count}} objects are too many to draw. Pick one or more namespaces in the top bar.
topology.unavailable: Not shown (no permission or not synced yet): {{kinds}}
topology.empty: No objects in the selected namespaces
topology.clickHint: Click an object to highlight what it depends on and what depends on it; double-click to open it. Scroll to zoom, drag to move.

explain.title: Explain {{name}}
explain.thinking: Gathering the object's state, events and logs and asking the AI…
explain.error: The explanation could not be generated
explain.redactionNote: Env values, Secret data and secret-looking text were removed before sending. The redaction is a heuristic: review your workloads if they log credentials.
explain.disclaimer: Generated by AI: check it before acting

assistant.title: AI assistant
assistant.intro: Ask about your clusters: what is failing, why a pod restarts, what is deployed where. It looks things up with your permissions and never changes anything.
assistant.privacy: Questions and the data it reads (with env values and secrets removed) go to the AI provider configured in Settings. Closing the panel forgets the conversation; each question is audited.
assistant.placeholder: Ask about this cluster… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)

suggest.restarts: Which pods keep restarting and why?
suggest.capacity: Is any node short of resources?
